latin.124:
§. IX.
Dorschei Canones reliqui, quibus Confessionem Philippicam, privata tantum Auctoritate, non etiam publica Subsequente factam, quin, publicâ Auctoritate improbatam rejectamque, esse, innuit,
latin.125: praeterquam quòd, ab Auctoribus supra allegatis, sigillatim Joh. Crocio Comm. Cap. LVI. pag. 746. ab ipso etiam Mentzero Lutherano, non agnoscuntur,
latin.126: ita ex ipso Dorscheo falsitatis arguuntur, per jam tum retrò memoratarum ad Ferdinandum I. Imperatorem, à Statibus Imperii datarum & a Dorscheo pagina 20. integra in vernacula nostra lingua recensitarum literarum, verba sequentia:
latin.127: Gleichergestalt wollen wir auch hiemit die Apologi/ so durch unsere Vorfahren/ und zum theil uns /auf gemeltem Reichs Tag zu Augspurg/ überreichet / aber man nicht hat annehmen wollen/wie die selbige hernach zu Wittenberg gedruckt/und auf gedachtem Colloquio zu Wormbs A. 1540. neben obberührten verbesserten Confession übergeben / ausdrucklich repetirt und uns darzu bekennt haben.
latin.128: Wie denn auch gleicher gestalt unsere Meinung dahin gericht / daß wir andere der unsere Schrifften und repetirte Confessionen/ so der Kays: Maj. aufgehaltenen Reichs-Tagen und Colloquien/durch die Ständ/unserer Religion/zu weiterer Erklärung der beständigen und unwiederlegten Warheit / und Abwendung deren eine lange Zeit eingerissenen falschen Lehren und Mißbrauchen übergeben / und zum Theil publiciret/ hiemit nicht verwerffen / noch begeben / sondern dieselbe/im Verstand der heiligen Schrifft und ieko erneurter Augspurgischen Confession und Apologi gemäß/in alle Weg wollen vorbehalten haben. Da auch unser Gegentheil etliche Articul oder Wörter in dieser Augspurgischen Confession und Apologi / welche zum Anfang dieser hochnothwendigen / unvermeidentlichen Veränderung / zum Theil/ auch nach Art und Gebrauch der Teutschen Sprachen zu reden / zum glimpfligsten gestellt / und sonderlich da vom H. Sacrament und Messe / auch von der Römischen Kirchen gemelt wird / zu ihrem Vortheil und dahin deuten oder ziehen wolten / als wenn wir auch mit ihren abgöttischen Lehren und Ceremonien/in denen sich gleichwol nachgehends allerhand Christliche Aenderungen zugetragen / der Päpstischen Kirchen /und sonderlich dem Greuel der transubstantiation , der Päpstischen Meß / und was dem anhängig / einig/ so erklären wir uns hiemit abermal / daß es die Meinung gar nicht hat / &c.
latin.129: & post. Hinwiderum aber ist unser Meinung und Fürsatz gar nicht/ daß wir in unsern Landen/ Gebieten / Kirchen / und Schulen einige andere Lehr / denn die / wie obgemelt/ in der heiligen göttlichen Schrifft gegründet/und der Augspurgischen Confession und Apologi in ihrem rechten Verstand gemäß / dulden oder vertheidigen/ sondern uns allein zu der erkanten Warheit bekennen/ und nichts / so derselben entgegen/ einreissen lassen / oder gestatten wollen. &c. Confer. Historiam Conventus Nauenburgici hôc ipso anno in vernacula nostra denuo recensitam a Dn. D. Hönnio, Consiliario Saxonico Ducali ac Secretario intimo pag. 103. 105. 106. 107.

pass_a.124: Paragraph nine. Dorsche's remaining canons, by which he hints that the Philippica Confession was made by private authority alone, not also by subsequent public authority, and even that it was condemned and rejected by public authority,
pass_a.125: besides that they are not acknowledged by the authors cited above, especially by John Crocius in his Commentary chapter 56 page 746, and even by Mentzer the Lutheran himself,
pass_a.126: so they are convicted of falsehood from Dorsche himself, by the letters already mentioned back then to Emperor Ferdinand I, given by the Estates of the Empire and reviewed in full by Dorsche at page 20 in our vernacular tongue, in the following words:
pass_a.127: Likewise we also hereby affirm the Apology which through our ancestors and partly through us was presented at the said Imperial Diet at Augsburg but which they would not accept, as the same was afterward printed at Wittenberg and at the said Colloquy at Worms in the year 1540 was handed over beside the aforementioned improved Confession, expressly repeated and we have confessed ourselves to it.
pass_a.128: As then also in like manner our mind is directed to this, that we do not hereby reject or surrender other of our writings and repeated Confessions which at Imperial Diets and Colloquies held by His Imperial Majesty the Estates of our Religion delivered for further explanation of the constant and irrefutable truth and for turning away false teachings and abuses that had long broken in, and partly published; but we will in every way reserve the same according to the sense of holy Scripture and of the now renewed Augsburg Confession and Apology. And since our opponents would also twist some articles or words in this Augsburg Confession and Apology which at the beginning of this highly necessary unavoidable change were partly set in the mildest way also after the manner and use of the German tongue to speak, and especially where the holy Sacrament and Mass and also the Roman Church are mentioned, to their advantage and as if we were one with their idolatrous teachings and ceremonies of the papal Church in which nonetheless afterward all sorts of Christian changes occurred, and especially with the horror of transubstantiation, the papal Mass, and what hangs on it, so we declare ourselves hereby again that that is not the meaning at all, and so on.
pass_a.129: And afterward. But on the contrary our mind and purpose is not at all that we in our lands, territories, churches, and schools should tolerate or defend any other teaching than that which, as said above, is grounded in the holy divine Scripture and accords with the Augsburg Confession and Apology in their right sense; but that we confess ourselves to the recognized truth alone and will let nothing contrary to it break in or permit it, and so on. Compare the History of the Naumburg Convention reviewed again this very year in our vernacular by the lord Doctor Hoennius, Ducal Saxon councillor and intimate secretary, pages 103, 105, 106, 107.

124: §. IX. Dorsche's remaining canons hint that the Philippica Confession rested on private authority alone — not on later public authority — and was even condemned and rejected by public authority.
125: Besides, the authors already cited do not own those canons — least of all John Crocius (Commentary, ch. 56, p. 746), and not even Mentzer the Lutheran.
126: So Dorsche himself convicts them of falsehood: the letter already named — from the Imperial Estates to Emperor Ferdinand I — which he prints in full in our vernacular at page 20, runs as follows:
127: Likewise we hereby also hold the Apology which our ancestors — and partly we ourselves — presented at that Augsburg Diet, though it was not accepted; afterward it was printed at Wittenberg, and at the Worms Colloquy in 1540 it was delivered beside the improved Confession already named — expressly repeated, and we have confessed ourselves to it.
128: In the same way our mind is this: we do not reject or give up our other writings and repeated Confessions — those the Estates of our religion handed in at Imperial Diets and colloquies under His Majesty, partly published, to explain the standing, unrefuted truth and to drive out long-settled false teaching and abuse.
We mean to keep them in every way in the sense of holy Scripture and of the now-renewed Augsburg Confession and Apology.

And when our opponents twist some early, mild articles or words in that Confession and Apology — set gently, partly in German speech-habit, especially where the holy Sacrament, the Mass, and the Roman Church are named — as if we agreed with their idolatrous papal teachings and ceremonies (in which Christian changes later came anyway), and above all with the horror of transubstantiation, the papal Mass, and what hangs on it: we declare again that this is not our meaning at all.
129: And afterward: on the contrary, it is not our mind or purpose to tolerate or defend in our lands, territories, churches, and schools any teaching other than what is grounded, as said above, in holy Scripture and fits the Augsburg Confession and Apology in their right sense.
We mean to confess the known truth alone, and to let nothing against it break in or be allowed.
Compare the History of the Naumburg Convention, reviewed again this very year in our vernacular by Dr. Hoennius, Ducal Saxon councillor and intimate secretary (pp. 103, 105, 106, 107).
